Distribution. There is very limited information in order to define the range of this Mexican endemism, but the two known localities are relatively close in the states of Guanajuato and Michoacán, in two areas of the central distribution of the Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt Pine-Oak Forest biome separated by the Bajío Dry Forest (Fig. 6, white circles). The species is rare in the collections that I studied and presumably has a reduced geographic and ecological range.

d.a: Distribution and habitat. Oreonectes jinxiuensis sp. nov. is currently known from Jinxiu Town, Yao Autonomous County, Laibin City (24.120353 ° N, 110.214124 ° E) (Fig. 3 A), and Xiuren Town, Lipu City, Guilin (probably), Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China; mainly distributed in the Liujiang River system of the Pearl River basin in the Dayao Mountains area. This species inhabits small streamlets with water depths of about 0.5 m, characterized by abundant rocks and macrophytes around, providing good habitat for Oreonectes jinxiuensis sp. nov. (Fig. 3 B). Other species present in the streamlet include Acrossocheilus parallens, Rhinogobius giurinus, and Opsariichthys bidens. Comparisons Genetic comparisons. BI analysis of the constructed phylogenetic tree, based on a concatenated dataset of COI and Cyt b sequences, revealed consistent topologies. The phylogenetic tree confirmed the validity of the new species with high nodal support (BPP ≥ 0.95). Additionally, species within Oreonectes formed a monophyletic group, phylogenetically sister to the clade containing Guinemachilus and Micronemacheilus. Oreonectes jinxiuensis sp. nov. formed a highly supported clade with O. guilinensis and O. platycephalus (Fig. 4). However, the O. platycephalus sequence DQ 105197 forms a distinct lineage separate from other O. platycephalus sequences in the phylogenetic tree. The taxonomic validity of this sequence requires further verification, and DQ 105197 was not included in this study’s sample and does not represent O. platycephalus discussed herein. Genetic distances within the genus Oreonectes were calculated based on a concatenated dataset of mitochondrial COI and Cyt b (Table 4). The uncorrected p - distances between the new species and its congeners ranged from 4.1 % (O. guilinensis) to 10.6 % (O. guananensis), similar to values between other species in the same genus, such as 4.4 % between O. damingshanensis and O. zhangi, 4.7 % between O. qinae and O. zhangi, and 5.3 % between O. guananensis and O. luochengensis. Despite the close phylogenetic position of Oreonectes jinxiuensis sp. nov. and O. platycephalus on the BI tree, the p - distance between them (calculated using sequences ON 116528 and OR 396957, excluding DQ 105197) was 7.8 %. Substantial genetic divergence supports the conclusion that Oreonectes jinxiuensis sp. nov. represents a distinct species. Morphological comparisons. Based on the results of PCA, two principal components of the morphological characters of Oreonectes jinxiuensis sp. nov. and O. guilinensis and O. platycephalus, which are phylogenetically close congeners of the new species, were extracted (Table 5). In the comparison between O. jinxiuensis sp. nov. and O. guilinensis and O. platycephalus (Fig. 5), the first principal component (PC 1), which accounted for 39.6 % of the variance, was influenced by predorsal length, pelvic length, pectoral-fin length, caudal-peduncle length, interorbital length; the second principal component (PC 2), which accounted for 24.5 % of the variance, was influenced by standard length, prepelvic length, preanal length, preanus length, postorbital length. Oreonectes jinxiuensis sp. nov. can be distinguished from O. guilinensis by swim bladder degenerated (vs. developed), 8 – 16 lateral-line pores (vs. 4 – 6), a short tube (less than half the length of posterior chamber) connected two chamber of swim bladder (vs. a long, slender tube, exceeding half the length of posterior chamber and nearly equal to its full length), four unbranched and seven branched dorsal-fin rays (vs. two unbranched and six branched dorsal-fin rays), body width at front of dorsal fin 12.9 % – 16.0 % of SL (vs. 16.8 % – 18.8 %), body width at front of anal fin 5.8 % – 9.7 % of SL (vs. 10.5 % – 12.3 %), preanal length 73.7 % – 77.3 % of SL (vs. 77.5 % – 78.8 %), preanus length 66.1 % – 71.2 % of SL (vs. 72.1 % – 73.0 %), caudal-peduncle depth 12.5 % – 13.8 % of SL (vs. 10.5 % – 11.5 %), dorsal fin base to pelvic fin base 28.1 % – 32.0 % of SL (vs. 33.0 % – 35.9 %), pectoral fin length 18.1 % – 21.6 % of SL (vs. 14.6 % – 16.6 %), pelvic length 15.6 % – 18.7 % of SL (vs. 11.5 % – 13.4 %), eye diameter 16.4 % – 20.3 % of HL (vs. 12.1 % – 16.1 %). Oreonectes jinxiuensis sp. nov. can be distinguished from O. platycephalus by four unbranched and seven branched dorsal-fin rays (vs. three unbranched and six branched dorsal-fin rays), six branched pelvic fin rays (vs. seven), a dark brown lateral stripe on both body sides presence (vs. absence), body width at front of dorsal fin 12.9 % – 16.0 % of SL (vs. 5.7 % – 10.8 %), head length 21.1 % – 24.3 % of SL (vs. 15.5 % – 19.4 %), caudal-peduncle length 13.3 % – 16.1 % of SL (vs. 10.2 % – 12.9 %), head width 15.3 % – 18.4 % of SL (vs. 10.7 % – 13.4 %). Morphological data of O. platycephalus following Ito (2024). Oreonectes jinxiuensis sp. nov. formed a highly supported clade with O. guilinensis and O. platycephalus. Both p - distance and morphological data support the separation of the new species from these two species.
